items.title: FBI reportedly hacked again, this time targeting nationwide police database
items.summary: FBI systems have reportedly been breached for the second time in two months, this time targeting the agency's National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which is used to share information between local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. [...]

items.title: Chess.com’s next move is a new hub for classic games, from mahjong to sudoku
items.summary: Chess.com is ready to go a lot bigger than chess. After launching Gambit, a gambling-free poker site, earlier this year, the company is now adding 10 more games: backgammon, checkers, go, hearts, mahjong, shogi, sudoku, solitaire, xiangqi, and a Scrabble alternative called word. They're all part of Chess's new Classic Games platform, which is launching […]

items.title: Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day
items.summary:
A threat actor used autonomous Cairn AI agents to discover and exploit a critical MONAI Label vulnerability.
The post Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
items.summary:
A malicious webpage could extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories from the assistant without triggering any approval prompt, researchers have shown.

The same attack could be extended to reach the credentials Muse stores for the user's connected accounts.

items.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
items.summary:
A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG.

The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions.

The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, affects all software that uses GPGME before version 2.3.0,

items.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
items.summary:
Suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging server, and gain root access to a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence said this week.

The flaw allows an attacker with no account to write files outside the server's storage folder, and it affects MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier in the default setup,

items.title: Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS
items.summary:
Signal has announced that it will restrict screenshots by default to stop artificial intelligence (AI) agents from reading private chats on Android and iOS devices, but conceded that the protection is "incomplete."
